source_review.notes: Checked official NASA Risk Management Handbook v2 Parts 1 and 2; current NPR 8000.4C chapters 1 and 3 and Appendix C; current Technical Risk Management guidance; active GSFC-HDBK-8005 record; current NASA Safety and Mission Assurance risk-management overview; Software Engineering Handbook CRM guidance; and current NODIS directive status. All ten final reference URLs returned HTTP 200. An obsolete IV&V PDF URL initially returned 404 and was replaced before review completion with the current official SMA overview. The chapter follows objectives-driven scenario identification, structured risk statements, explicit uncertainty and governance, and cross-cutting/inherited risk coordination.

evidence: Reviewed risk tuple, causal sequence, expected consequence, time-indexed risk identity, dependency graph, and conditional expected-consequence relation.
Confirmed objectives, baseline, scenarios, likelihood, consequence vector, uncertainty, evidence, timeframe, governance, status and history are separately defined.
Confirmed causal arrows are explicitly hypotheses rather than deterministic implications and expected consequence is limited to valid probabilities/cardinal consequences.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation prevents a register cell or ordinal score from replacing scenario, evidence, uncertainty, timing and governance.

evidence: Executed risk-register-structure-check and reproduced three risks, one separate issue, unique IDs, three structured statements/objective links/owners/triggers/current records, two dependency edges, zero orphan edges, and structurally complete status.
Recomputed the ordinal-matrix teaching example 2 times 5 and 5 times 2 as equal numeric products of 10 while confirming that equality has no justified risk-equivalence semantics.
Confirmed issue records are excluded from risk_count and graph edges resolve only to declared risk identifiers.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The executable checker audits declared structural fields/links only and does not quantify or validate the risks.

evidence: Confirmed the structured condition-to-departure-to-asset/objective-to-consequence sequence matches the generic risk-statement logic without asserting certainty.
Confirmed expected consequence summation requires mutually exclusive or otherwise coherently modeled scenarios and cardinal consequence on a common basis.
Confirmed the dependency graph can encode causal, shared-resource, temporal and informational edges but requires typed/directed evidence for interpretation.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No ordinal likelihood/consequence category is multiplied, averaged or summed as a valid cardinal measure in the chapter.

evidence: Challenged vague topics, consequence-only statements, mitigation-embedded statements, tautologies, present issues disguised as future events, assumptions treated as facts, mega-risks, duplicates, and over-decomposition/double counting.

Reviewed hazards, intentional threats/conditional likelihood, vulnerabilities, opportunities, interface/inherited/cross-cutting risks, common causes, mutually exclusive/cascading scenarios, provider/acquirer boundaries, and false transfer.

Reviewed ordinal matrix misuse, domain vetoes, low-likelihood catastrophic cases, owner without authority/resources, elevation abandonment, sensitive records, stale reviews, false closure, deleted history, and incentives suppressing dissent.
Reviewed all ten examples and five answers for objectives, causal mechanisms, evidence, uncertainty, timing, dependencies, affected stakeholders, governance, access, change and bounded claims.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Consequential applications still require applicable safety, security, privacy, human-factors, ethics, legal, environmental, cost/schedule, supplier, operations, public-health, community and affected-stakeholder review.

evidence: Traced objective/baseline linkage, continuous identification, causal statement structure, issue separation, stable identity/history, narrative evidence, governed scale semantics, explicit roles/authority, dependency/common-cause representation, sensitive handling and health-over-row-count throughout the module.
Confirmed stable IDs survive revisions and merges/splits/closures preserve links and evidence rather than deleting history.
Confirmed action owner, risk owner, acceptance authority, provider/acquirer and elevation roles remain distinct.
Confirmed change, incidents, anomalies, test, model, supplier, operation and stakeholder evidence trigger controlled update/reidentification.
invariant_checking.notes: Register structural completeness is consistently treated as necessary but insufficient for identification completeness, analytical credibility or acceptable risk.

proof_review.notes: The chapter presents risk representations and conditional expectation but no theorem proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Reviewed credible, complete, current, controlled, independent, accepted, closed, safe, secure, representative, comprehensive, calibrated and validated language for explicit evidence scope.
artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-047/report.json records exact local execution evidence for declared register fields and links only.

Incident, anomaly, test, supplier, model, forecast, interview, workshop, hazard, threat, operational, historical and stakeholder evidence remains qualified by configuration, source, uncertainty, applicability, conflicts and limitations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No external review is claimed. A structurally complete register, low score, green cell, completed action or independent review is never presented as proof that risks are complete, controlled or acceptable.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked objective, risk, condition, departure, asset, consequence, statement/narrative, register, issue, hazard, threat, vulnerability, opportunity, owner and inherited/interface/cross-cutting risk. Scenario, likelihood, consequence, uncertainty, issue, control, ownership, action and acceptance remain distinct.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked topic-to-scenario conversion, issue/residual risk, shared assumptions, mega-risk splitting, ordinal matrix caution, interface ownership, opportunities, sensitive security, false closure, register-health audits, database migration, certificate services, rail signaling and heat-health response. Each ties causal evidence to decision roles and change.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from objectives/semantics through causal statements/narratives, issue/hazard/threat/assumption distinctions, multi-lens methods and speaking-up, interface/inherited risks, decomposition, schema/history, analysis/scales/prioritization/dependence, roles/elevation/access, freshness/coverage/health/communication and learning.
